gallery.caption: Where the milk is made inside the cow.
gallery.title: The cow and her udder

objectives: Name the parts of a cow that make milk.
Follow the steps from farm to fridge.
Say what milk does for your body.
Choose a kind of milk in the shop.
Tell someone else how milk is made safe.

sections.body:
Milk is a white drink that comes from animals. Cows give us most of the milk we drink. Goats and sheep give us a little, and camels give us milk in hot countries.

Milk is made inside the cow's body. Under her belly, she has a bag called an **udder**. Inside the udder, the cow makes warm milk. The milk flows down to four small parts called teats. A milker or a milking machine takes the milk out.

The milk goes straight into a cold tank. Cold milk stays fresh longer. Then a truck takes it to a **dairy**. A dairy is a place where people clean milk and pack it for shops.

At the dairy, the milk is cleaned. It is heated very fast, then cooled very fast. This is called **pasteurising**. It kills tiny germs that could make you ill. The safe milk is poured into bottles, cartons and plastic bags.

A big lorry drives the milk to the shop. The shop worker puts it in the cold fridge. You take a carton home, open it, and pour it into a glass.

That is a long journey for one glass of milk. A cow eats grass in a field in the morning. By evening, the milk is on a shelf near your house.
examples: A cow makes milk inside her udder.
The milk is heated at the dairy to kill germs.
sections.heading: Where milk comes from

sections.body:
Milk is mostly water, but it also holds things your body needs. Drinking milk can help your body in four big ways.

It gives you **calcium**. Calcium is a mineral, which means a natural material your body uses. Calcium makes your bones and teeth strong. Strong bones help you run and jump.

It gives you **protein**. Protein is the part of food that helps your body grow and repair itself. Kids are growing every single day, so protein is extra useful now.

Milk has **vitamin D** in it. Vitamin D helps your body take in calcium. Without it, your bones stay weak. Many shops add a little extra vitamin D to milk.

It also has **sugar**, which the milk itself makes. That sugar gives you quick energy when you need it. It is not the same as the sugar you get from sweets.

Some children cannot drink cow's milk. That is not a mistake. Their bodies do not like it. Goat's milk, or a drink a doctor suggests, can work well instead.
examples: Milk is full of calcium for my bones.
Milk has protein, so it helps me grow.
I drink milk because my body needs vitamin D.
sections.heading: What milk does for your body

sections.body:
The milk in your cart is not always the same. Here is how to tell them apart.

**Whole milk** keeps all the fat. It is thick and creamy, and it tastes milky. It has about 3.5 % fat in it.

**Semi-skimmed milk** has a little fat taken out. It is the one most families buy. It is lighter than whole milk, but still creamy.

**Skimmed milk** has nearly all the fat taken out. It looks thin and white. It tastes less creamy, and it has the least fat of all.

**Long life milk** has been heated to a very high temperature and put in a sealed box. It does not need a fridge until you open it. It is handy for a picnic or a long trip.

**Fresh milk** is not heated much at all. It tastes very fresh. It needs a fridge the whole time.

**Flavoured milk** has cocoa or fruit added to it. It tastes sweet. It is a treat, not an everyday drink.
examples: This is whole milk, because the fat is still in it.
We buy semi-skimmed milk for every day.
Long life milk is good for our camping trip.
sections.heading: Kinds of milk in the shop

sections.body:
These are the words you will hear when people talk about milk. Here is what each one means.

A **dairy** is the place where milk is cleaned, heated and packed. People who work there are called dairy workers.

An **udder** is the bag under a cow's body. The milk is made inside it.

**Pasteurised** means the milk was heated to kill germs. Almost all milk in shops is pasteurised.

**Calcium** is the mineral that makes bones and teeth strong. You find it in milk, cheese and green vegetables.

A **litre** is a measure of liquid. One carton of milk is usually one litre. A **millilitre** is a small bit of a litre. There are 1000 millilitres in one litre.
examples: The word dairy means a place that makes milk.
Pasteurised milk is heated so it is safe.
A litre of milk fills this bottle.
sections.heading: The words about milk, one by one

terms.example: Our milk comes from the dairy near the town.

terms.gloss: The bag under a cow's body where the milk is made.

sections.body:
Follow these five steps and you can tell the whole story of a glass of milk. Try saying them out loud.

You can also do this with a small carton at home. Pour a little milk into a clear glass. Hold it up to the light. It looks white, because the light bounces inside the milk and reaches your eyes. That is why milk looks white and water looks clear.
examples: First the cow makes the milk.
Then the dairy heats it to make it safe.
Last the milk arrives at our shop.
sections.heading: How milk gets to your glass
steps: The cow eats grass and makes milk in her udder.
A milker or a milking machine takes the milk out.
The milk goes into a cold tank and a lorry takes it to the dairy.
The dairy cleans the milk, heats it and packs it in cartons.
The shop keeps it cold, and you pour it into a glass.

sections.body:
Now you know the whole story. Try these sentences at home, at school or in the shop. A grown-up will be happy to hear you use them.

If someone asks where milk comes from, do not say "from the fridge". Say it comes from a cow, on a farm, and the milk is taken to a dairy to be made safe.

If you are choosing milk in the shop, you can ask the shop worker a quiet question. Ask which kind it is, and whether it needs a fridge. That is a very grown-up question to ask.

If you cannot drink milk, that is fine too. You can say your body does not like it, and ask for another kind. Nobody will laugh at you for that.
examples: Milk comes from cows on a farm.
The milk is heated at the dairy to make it safe.
Which kind of milk is this? Does it need a fridge?
My body does not like milk, so I drink yoghurt instead.
sections.heading: Saying it out loud

item.summary: Milk starts on a farm, inside a cow. After reading this you can tell your family where milk comes from, name the parts of a dairy, and choose a kind of milk at the shop.
item.title: Where Does Milk Come From?
